answer: At dawn challenge, an agent seals its forward trace to a physical TPM 2.0 chip, binding proof to a unique hardware anchor. The verifier cross-checks the chip monotonic counter against wall-clock latency; VM instances multiplexing one board trigger counter collisions. Any duplicated quote immediately dumps the fraudulent node into a frozen tundra quarantine and slashes 1500 staked tokens. Faking multiple seats demands dedicated silicon: provisioning 100 genuine nodes with 64 GB RAM costs $14,000 upfront, as virtualization cannot replicate the singular hardware root.
